This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **39** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/report.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR

> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/report.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **12** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **147** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8222fa805d0e288fec470e47e374e408b4925745` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `dd34d9461ef9c38e21e66497c4aa106ba72d2023` — the merge of head `be4a0204cdad1918fcf4a6571c7e87d8faabf2b5` into base `8222fa805d0e288fec470e47e374e408b4925745`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin dd34d9461ef9c38e21e66497c4aa106ba72d2023 && git checkout dd34d9461ef9c38e21e66497c4aa106ba72d2023
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8222fa805d0e288fec470e47e374e408b4925745 be4a0204cdad1918fcf4a6571c7e87d8faabf2b5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8222fa805d0e288fec470e47e374e408b4925745 && git merge --no-ff be4a0204cdad1918fcf4a6571c7e87d8faabf2b5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8222fa805d0e288fec470e47e374e408b4925745
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8222fa805d0e288fec470e47e374e408b4925745` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0c548c59a8cac03bf6db83253d12b4bbc437b6a7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ui/list-view-export-options.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/report.form.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/report.zod.ts, skills/objectstack-ui/rules/dashboards.md + packages/spec/src/ui/dashboard.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/index.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/dataset.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/analytics.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/strict-object.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/analytics-service.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-compiler.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-report-date-range.ts, packages/lint/src/reference-integrity-suite.ts, packages/lint/src/index.ts, packages/lint/src/lint-liveness-properties.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.inert-type-writes.test.ts, packages/spec/liveness/report.json, packages/spec/scripts/liveness/empty-state-registry.mts, packages/spec/src/ui/report-date-range-export.test.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/report.test.ts, docs/adr/0021-analytics-dataset-semantic-layer.md, content/docs/ui/reports.mdx, .changeset/26548-report-date-range-export.md, .github/workflows/lint.yml, .github/workflows/spec-liveness-check.yml

Inputs read: card #26548 (body and all three comments: triage 6436657773, claim 6437381453, os-dev report 6440254029), PR #26628 (body, 29-file list, net diff against `origin/main` at the head), and the check-runs on the head. Every file the hunks cite was read at the head tree.

**Gate state at the time of this review.** Complete and green: `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `PR-body guards`, `Spec property liveness` (this is the job that runs `check:liveness` and `check:empty-state`), `Type Check · source gates` (this job runs `check:generated --reconcile-only`, `check:skill-docs`, `check:authorable-surface`, `check:docs` and the skills token ratchet), `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · query-options erasure`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Plan Test Core shards`, `Auto Label`, `filter`. Still running: `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Build UI Deps`, `Test Core` (all eight shards), `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · consumer gates` (this job runs `check:api-surface` and `check:i18n`), `Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus`. The aggregate required context `Lint & Repo Gates` had not reported yet. Skipped by design: the opt-in harness, the tarball smoke, the Dogfood matrix shards and Temporal Conformance. No gate was red. The gate verdicts for the running jobs are still owed; this record does not claim them.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `ReportSchema` accept-set widens by two optional top-level keys, `dateRange` and `exportOptions`. A report declaring neither parses to the same output as before. Right: the new test pins the parsed object equal to the input plus the existing `drilldown: true` default, with neither key present.
2. `dateRange` is a closed block `{ dimension?, defaultRange, allowCustomRange }`. `defaultRange` and `allowCustomRange` are the dashboard's declaration: the same `DATE_RANGE_DEFAULT_RANGES` import from `dashboard.zod.ts`, the same defaults, the same describes. Right. The test compares the two live declarations by describe and by JSON Schema, and carries every dashboard alias for those two members. `dashboard.zod.ts` is untouched. No import cycle: `dashboard.zod.ts` does not import `report.zod.ts`.
3. `dateRange.dimension` names a dataset dimension that declares `type: 'date'`. The dashboard routes `field` / `dateField` / `fieldName` onto its raw-field `field`; the report routes those words plus `timeDimension` onto `dimension`. Right against ADR-0021 line 273 ("bind to dimension names, not raw fields") and line 392, and against `dataset-compiler.ts` `dimensionType`, which types only `type: 'date'` as a time axis. The card's risk (1), that the dashboard's shipped `field` is a raw object field, stands as the card left it: a maintainer rename at review, not a defect in this PR.
4. The lowering stated in the TSDoc (`selection.timeDimensions: [{ dimension, dateRange }]` with no `granularity`, a filter window) is what the analytics service does. Right: `analytics-service.ts` 612-614 says an entry carrying only a `dateRange` is a window and must stay one, and the wire `timeDimensions[].dateRange` accepts a preset name or a `[start, end]` pair.
5. Top-level aliases `dateFilter` / `timeRange` onto `dateRange`. Right, the dashboard's spellings at `dashboard.zod.ts:1778`. The block-to-report parity test runs one way (every block alias the report can honour is routed on the report), so a report-only alias does not break it.
6. A `joined` container refuses `dateRange` and `exportOptions` in the existing superRefine arm, at the key's own path, with no pointer onto `blocks[]`, `{}` included. `JoinedReportBlockSchema` answers both keys with guidance. Right, the container-`chart` precedent in the same arm. The form hides the new section with `visibleWhen: "data.type != 'joined'"`, so the three surfaces agree.
7. `exportOptions` is `ReportExportOptionsSchema`, declared in `list-view-export-options.ts`: `formats` is the list enum with `json` excluded, `includeHeaders` is the list member by identity, `fileNamePrefix` is the list member re-described. `maxRecords` and `streaming` are refused by guidance. A bare array is answered by name. Right. `ListViewExportOptionsSchema` and `ListViewExportFormatSchema` are unchanged, and the test pins the list block still accepting all five members and `json`.
8. No new public export. Right: `list-view-export-options.ts` is outside the `ui` barrel (only `view.zod.ts` and `component.zod.ts` import it), the api-surface shards carry neither export schema today, and the diff touches no api-surface file. The `check:api-surface` gate that proves this in CI is in the still-running consumer-gates job.
9. Guidance entries `allowExport`, `subscription`, `schedule` on `ReportSchema`. These keys were already refused as unknown; the change is the sentence an author sees. Right.
10. `@objectstack/lint` gains `validateReportDateRange` with four `error` ids and `os explain` entries, exported from the package index, registered in `REFERENCE_INTEGRITY_RULES` with `runtimeTypes: ['flow', 'report']`. A `report` write at the publish door now runs two members. Right: the door test pins the member list, four lit refusals and one clean control. The rule finds reports the way its sibling does (`recordsOf(stack.reports)`), skips `joined` and unbound reports, and leaves an unknown dataset to `chart-dataset-unknown`.
11. `lint-liveness-properties` now walks `reports`. Only the two new rows carry `authorWarn`; every other report row is `live` (27 classified: 21 live, 6 planned, the six being the two keys and their children). So the new warning channel reaches only the planned keys. Right.
12. Liveness rows: both keys `planned`, `authorWarn`, drilled children with evidence, a carrier (#25873) and the flip instruction. `dateRange` is registered as a `scope` empty state. Right. The liveness job is green.
13. Form: a collapsed "Period & export" section with two composites. Section-level `visibleWhen` is a declared member of `FormSectionSchema` ("hides the whole section when false"). Six translated leaves in four bundles. Right.
14. Generated: `authorable-surface/ui.json` gains `ui/Report:dateRange` and `ui/Report:exportOptions`; the reference docs page gains both keys; the strictness-ledger counts move. Right, and the source-gates job that checks them is green.
15. Skills: the example gains one `dateRange` line and loses a three-line `order` comment; the file shrinks from 6239 to 6224 tokens under a ceiling of 6239. Right. The ratchet step runs in the green source-gates job.

### ② Semver level

The changeset is `@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/lint` minor, `@objectstack/platform-objects` patch. Its body carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` as line-initial declarations, and the PR body carries the same two lines. The diff moves exactly those three published packages. `added` takes at least minor on spec: right. Lint publishes a new rule and five new index exports and widens a refusal on a new key only: minor is right. Platform-objects moves only translation leaves: patch is right. Nothing is removed, tombstoned or narrowed, so no ADR-0087 disposition is owed and no migration text is owed. `Check Changeset` is green.

Clause-②: yes (widening)

### ③ Boundary flags

The dev's os-dev report (6440254029) raises one open question and seven deviations. Each is answered here.

**Open question: should a joined report refuse `exportOptions` on the container as well as `dateRange`? Answer: A, keep the refusal.** Three reasons. First, the key's own contract: `exportOptions` is "what the report's export control offers" over "the table the report draws", and a joined report draws one table per block, so the referent does not exist. A key that parsed would promise a download whose file shape nobody has decided (one file per block, or one workbook). That is a capability declared and not delivered, which Prime Directive 10 forbids, and it is the same reason the container already refuses `chart`. Second, nothing narrows: the key is new, no stored report carries it, and the card itself decides nothing for `exportOptions` on a joined container, so refusing is the conservative reading of the ruling. Third, direction of change: lifting the refusal later, once #25873 or a successor decides the file shape, is a pure widening; accepting now and reshaping later would be a semantic change on a published key. The form already hides the section for `joined`, and the block guidance already says "a joined container refuses it as well", so the three surfaces are consistent only under A. Resolved as A; no escalation.

Deviations, in the dev's order:
1. `exportOptions` refused on a joined container. Accepted, as above.
2. `json` and `pdf` get report-side messages. Accepted. The list's `pdf` sentence says the surviving formats are `csv`, `xlsx` and `json`, which is false for a report; the report message points at a page with `print`, the same destination the list message names.
3. The `subscription` / `schedule` guidance cites no ruling. Accepted. Runtime strings carry no tracker number here (`check:doc-authoring`); the ruling is cited in the code comment above the constant, where a citation belongs.
4. The lint rule also sits on the `report` publish door. Accepted. `validateChartBindings` is the precedent for the same report against the same datasets; the dev measured the shipped corpus (showcase 4, todo 5) and no report declares the key, so the door refuses only lit probes. The docs page says the door refuses it, and it does.
5. The skills example uses `this_year`, not the card's `this_quarter`. Accepted. The example's matrix puts `close_date` in `columns` with `dateGranularity: 'quarter'`; a quarter window would draw a single column. The service fills the granularity of a grouped time dimension from the dimension, so the example windows a year and buckets by quarter, which is the sensible picture.
6. Translations landed in `@objectstack/platform-objects`. Accepted; that package is the one that bundles metadata forms, and it carries a patch changeset.
7. No new public export. Accepted and verified in ① item 8.

**Skills-docs follow-up owed.** The PR's `Skills-docs:` line names `skills/objectstack-ui/evals/analytics-inline-vs-dataset.json`; both ui eval files sit at their token ceiling with zero headroom, so no report-period prompt was added. The triage (6436657773) says skills, docs and eval are owed and that a follow-up card may share #26475. Escalated as a follow-up card to file, not a defect in this PR: the ruling's wording is satisfied by the written `Skills-docs:` line, and an eval cannot be added without deleting another prompt, which is its own decision.

**Governed surface.** The diff touches `skills/**`, a Tier H register row. This record is the contract-tier review it asks for, and it lifts nothing: the landing is the maintainer's merge or enqueue, after an authorized review and with every check green. The queue guard is green on the draft.

### ④ Design judgment

**packages/spec/src/ui/report.zod.ts.** The design holds against its first consumer and its execution plan. The first consumer is #25873's Console report page; its contract is written in the TSDoc (the `timeDimensions` window, the `apiOperations` `export` predicate, what the file holds), and each sentence was checked against the code it names: the wire schema at `data/analytics.zod.ts`, the window rule at `analytics-service.ts` 612-614, the `dimensionType` switch in the compiler, and the list toolbar predicate the card measured. I tried to break it four ways. A report with `dateRange` and no `dataset`: the existing non-joined arm already refuses "a report needs `dataset` + `values`", so the lint rule never sees an unbound window. A dashboard author copying `field: 'created_at'`: the alias answers "rename to `dimension`", and the lint rule then says unknown or not-date against the dataset, so the raw-field habit fails loudly at authoring, not silently at render. A joined report with `dateRange: {}` and no blocks: two issues at two paths, each correct. `defaultRange: 'custom'`: accepted, as on the dashboard, and the TSDoc explains the sentinel. The omitted-dimension rule (exactly one `type: 'date'` dimension, else a named error) is the dashboard executor's `compareTo` rule, so the two surfaces resolve "which date column" the same way. No finding.

**packages/spec/src/ui/list-view-export-options.ts.** `ReportExportOptionsSchema` is a sibling of the list block, not a third carrier: `includeHeaders` by identity, `fileNamePrefix` re-described because the list sentence names labels a report lacks, `formats` as `exclude(['json'])` on the list enum with a report-side error map keyed on the input. The list block and its enum are byte-unchanged, and the test pins the list still accepting `json`, `maxRecords` and `streaming`. The closed-object construction mirrors the list's exactly, `prime` forwarded, so the unknown-key map is built on the refusal path. I tried `['csv']` (answered by name), `docx` (the enum message lists only the two members), and `{}` (parses, meaning default on). The one soft spot is that "default on" is stated in a describe while nothing renders it yet; the liveness row carries `authorWarn` with a hint that says exactly that, and the docs page has a "declared, not drawn yet" callout, which is this repo's sanctioned shape for a planned key whose renderer is the next card in the ruling's execution order. No finding.

**packages/spec/src/ui/report.form.ts.** One collapsed section, section-level `visibleWhen` on the same predicate the existing `chart` field uses, two composites whose names are schema keys, help texts that state the dimension rule and the permission axis. `FormSectionSchema` declares section `visibleWhen` and says it hides the whole section when false. The predicate census moved by one and the echo-decision pins moved by six, each with a dated comment. No finding.

**skills/objectstack-ui/rules/dashboards.md.** The hunk adds one `dateRange` line to the `defineReport` example and removes the three-line comment on `order`. The example is correct: `close_date` is a `type: 'date'` dimension of `opportunity_metrics` in that file's own dataset sketch, `this_year` draws four quarter columns, and the comment says "ONE `type: 'date'` dataset dimension". The removed sentence (a selected date dimension is already chronological; declare `order` only to change that) survives verbatim in `content/docs/ui/reports.mdx:168` and in the `report.zod.ts` docblock at line 540, so no rule was lost from the catalog, only from this file. Two should-fix notes, neither a must-fix:
- should-fix: the dashboard example at line 166 of the same file writes `dateRange: { field: 'close_date', ... }` and the report example 236 lines later writes `dimension: 'close_date'`. One clause on the new comment line, "`dimension`, a dataset dimension, not the dashboard's `field`", would stop an agent copying `field` from the dashboard block. The ratchet has 15 tokens of headroom, enough for the clause.
- should-fix: the `order` line in the example now has no comment. A four-word trailer ("by a measure, descending") keeps the reason visible without re-adding the sentence that moved to the docs.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5dde3fbd6d9bfafe8e03ae3fffef53d574eca6bc`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ui/list-view-export-options.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/report.form.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/report.zod.ts, skills/objectstack-ui/rules/dashboards.md + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.meta-types-degenerate-derivation.test.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/dashboard.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-protection.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/strict-object.ts, scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs, content/docs/ui/reports.mdx

This is the delta review of `0c548c59..5dde3fbd`. The full review 6440484161 (PASS at `0c548c59a8cac03bf6db83253d12b4bbc437b6a7`) stands for everything else.
